interest: This document is valuable as an archival index illustrating the U.S. State Department's tracking of unfree labor practices and humanitarian crises in interwar Japan. It highlights two distinct U.S. foreign policy and economic concerns during the 1930s: the trade implications of Japanese convict and compulsory labor under American tariff legislation, and the severe human toll of the Great Depression in rural Japan, where agricultural famine drove desperate families to sell daughters into servitude.
overview: This file consists of a single U.S. State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.5048 (covering slavery, compulsory labor, and peonage in Japan) spanning 1930 to 1934. The sheet lists two registered sub-items: a cross-reference noting a report from Tokyo by Bingham on Japanese convict and compulsory labor in relation to U.S. tariff provisions, and a November 24, 1934 submission by Dudley O. Paterson to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs enclosing a press report regarding the sale of approximately 60,000 girls into slavery by destitute parents in famine-affected areas of Japan.

subfiles.about: A Department of State list of papers indexing records on Japanese convict labor, slavery, and peonage.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes two entries under decimal file 894.5048 concerning labor and servitude in Japan. The first entry cross-references a March 27 report from Tokyo by Bingham concerning convict and other compulsory labor evaluated under U.S. tariff regulations. The second entry records a November 24, 1934 transmission from Dudley O. Paterson to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, enclosing an International News article describing how 60,000 girls were sold into slavery by starving parents in famine-stricken Japanese rural areas.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Slavery, Compulsory Labor, and Peonage in Japan (File 894.5048)
